extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, Department of the Interior / Bureau of Indian Affairs officials, tribal leaders and petitioning Indian groups, and attorneys handling federal recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Legislative text and hearing record establishing an administrative procedure and definitional criteria for the Department of the Interior to determine and acknowledge the existence of Indian tribes for a federal government-to-government relationship, including evidence types, procedural steps, timelines, and legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Indian identity (minimum 44 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has been identified as 'Indian', 'Native American', or 'Aboriginal' consistently and for a protracted period of time, but in any event for a period of no less than forty-four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence to be relied upon in determining continuing Indian identity shall include but not be limited to: (A) repeated identification as Indian by Federal authorities; (B) longstanding relations with State governments based on identification of the group as Indian; (C) repeated dealings with a county, parish, or other local governments in a unique relationship based on the group's Indian identity; (D) identification as Indian by records in courthouses, churches, or schools; (E) identification as Indian by anthropologists, historians, or other scholars; (F) identification as Indian in newspapers and books; and (G) any other evidence deemed relevant by the Office or the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longstanding tribal governmental influence or authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The group exhibits evidence of longstanding tribal governmental influence or authority over the members of the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This evidence shall show that the group has exercised political influence or authority over its members through a tribal council or other structure used as its own form of government or as a means to determine its membership. Such evidence may include traditional social or political structures or organizations unique to American Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of identified American Indian language or cultural retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The group utilizes an identified American Indian language or shows other clear indications of Indian cultural retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural markers (language use, ceremonies, practices) are admissible evidence supporting continuity of Indian identity; such cultural evidence may be used as one of the additional factors required for recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective rights in tribal lands or funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has held collective rights in tribal lands or funds, whether or not it expressly designated a tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession or exercise of collective rights in land or funds (even if not formally labeled 'tribal') supports recognition; documentation of collective property or communal financial arrangements is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition or treatment by other Indian tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has been treated as an Indian tribe by other Indian tribes or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor shall be evidenced by written statements from presently acknowledged tribes stating that they have related to the unacknowledged group for purposes connected with any intertribal activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty relations or formal governmental recognition historically
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has had treaty relations with the United States, particular States, or preexisting colonial or territorial governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Treaty relations" includes any formal relationship based on a government's acknowledgement of the Indian group's separate or distinct political status; such treaty or formal government relations shall be prima facie evidence of tribal existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation as Indian by Act of Congress or Executive order
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has been identified or referred to as an Indian tribe or designated Indian by an Act of Congress or Executive order which provided for, or otherwise affected or identified, the governmental structure, jurisdiction, or property of the tribal group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation by Congress or Executive order is prima facie evidence of tribal existence and carries special evidentiary weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance requirement across factors
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized, the group shall conform to factors (1) [continuing identity] and (2) [governmental influence] and at least one additional factor from the list in Section 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a threshold rule: satisfying both identity and governmental-influence factors is mandatory; claimants must also meet at least one other enumerated factor (3)-(7) to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and duties of a Special Investigative Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation within the Department of the Interior of a Special Investigative Office (the 'Office') to handle petitions: contact known unacknowledged groups, inform them of the right to petition, solicit statements, provide technical assistance, investigate historical background and Indian identity for verification, report findings to Congress and DOI leadership, assist in organization and enrollment, and refer concerns to appropriate agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office must contact all known groups within 12 months of enactment; all Bureau of Indian Affairs correspondence from unacknowledged groups shall be routed through the Office; the Office reviews petitions pending before BIA and allows petition revision; the Office may provide technical assistance for petition preparation and membership roll development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation standard — attention to Section 5 determinational factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations conducted or assisted by the Office must address the determinational factors set forth in Section 5 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All technical assistance and investigative activity must, at minimum, attend to the Section 5 factors (identity, governmental authority, and the additional enumerated factors) when verifying a group's historical background and Indian identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and report/response process for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within two years of receipt of a petition the Office shall submit a written preliminary report to the petitioning group; upon receipt the group has 60 days to respond; the Office then has thirty days to prepare a final report to the petitioner and the Secretary, which is to be published in the Federal Register; the Secretary shall adopt or reject the findings within six months following receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets mandatory procedural deadlines for preliminary report (2 years), petitioner response (60 days), final Office report (30 days after response), publication in Federal Register, and Secretary action (within 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of original filing date on petition amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall review petitions and allow the petitioning group to revise the petition if necessary to satisfy the guidelines; the effective date of the amended petition shall be that of the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may amend petitions without losing priority; this preserves original filing date for administrative processing and any time-based considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary determination, publication, and consequences of acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary determines on the basis of the report that the group is an Indian tribal entity under the Act, the Secretary shall designate such group as a federally acknowledged Indian tribe and, upon publication in the Federal Register, the tribe shall be entitled to the rights, privileges, immunities, benefits, and other services which other federally acknowledged Indian tribes are eligible to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Federal Register is the operative notice for federal acknowledgment and entitlement to federal programs and services; the Secretary's designation triggers eligibility for federal benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination, written reasons, judicial review and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Any termination by either the Office or the Secretary that a petitioning group is not an Indian tribe shall be in writing to the petitioning group and shall specify why the group does not conform to the definitional factors; any action by the Secretary shall be reviewable in the United States district court with the burden of proof on the United States to establish that the petitioners do not meet the criteria specified in this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions denying recognition must explain deficiencies; judicial review places burden on government (not petitioners) to prove nonconformity; this shifts litigation risk to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal fee provision where court affirms tribal existence
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal fees shall be paid by the United States to any petitioning group whose tribal existence is affirmatively determined as a matter of law and fact by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a court determines tribal existence in favor of petitioners, the US must pay legal fees — an incentive/relief provision for successful petitioners in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission allowed after denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial of any petition shall not preclude an Indian group from resubmitting a petition at any time in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial denial does not bar future petitions; groups retain ongoing opportunity to apply when additional evidence or circumstances change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership roll development and enrollment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon certification by the Secretary that a group is an Indian tribe, the tribe shall develop a membership roll; the process for determining the roll shall entail public notices, formation of tribal committees to hear claims, individuals' claims of direct tribal descent of a specified degree, and written statements of enrollment certification which must be recorded by the Bureau of Indian Affairs as well as by the tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office shall provide technical assistance for development of the roll at the request of the tribe; partial rolls are desirable prior to recognition to help verify tribal character, but the bill contemplates post-recognition roll development with BIA recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for some petition documentation (membership lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioning groups are expected to submit lists of current members and available former lists of members; for unrecognized groups seeking accountability and service delivery the Bureau believes a membership list is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIA regulations may require membership lists for accountability; the Department recommends partial membership documentation prior to recognition to verify government structure and membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual appropriations reporting on funds for newly acknowledged tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual budget requests for appropriations for any fiscal year from the Department of the Interior shall state the funds which have been directed to servicing those tribes whose existence was acknowledged in the preceding fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates an administrative transparency requirement linking recognition outcomes to budget reporting and appropriations justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's authority and administrative placement of recognition function
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior has authority to recognize additional Indian tribes; the bill establishes a separate Office but contemplates that such functions could be placed within the Bureau of Indian Affairs to use existing expertise and avoid unnecessary duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative confirmation of Secretary's authority is acceptable to DOI; administrative placement (separate Office vs. Bureau unit) should minimize duplication and utilize existing BIA staff and expertise.
